target-vector.t: Here is a vector **a**. Suppose we are only allowed to **move along one direction**.

direction.t: That direction is the **line through the vector b**. Which point on this line is **closest to a**?

drop-perpendicular.t: Drop a straight line from the tip of a down to the line, meeting it at a **right angle**. The shortest route is always perpendicular.

projection.t: Where the perpendicular lands is the **projection** of a onto b: the part of a that points **along b**.

residual.h: WHAT IS LEFT OVER: THE RESIDUAL
residual.t: The leftover part, **a minus its projection**, is the **residual**. It is **perpendicular to b**.

formula.t: The shadow's length comes from the dot product: **proj = ((a · b) / (b · b)) · b**.

ml-connection.t: The projection is the **closest point to a using only direction b**. Least squares and PCA are built on this idea.
